name: Vantablack Media Spectral Relay Shroud
description:
The Spectral Relay Shroud is a wearable signal architecture layered into a thin, flexible garment worn beneath street clothing — typically a vest or collar insert. It operates by fragmenting outgoing transmissions into thousands of microsecond-duration bursts, scattering them across seventeen discrete frequency bands simultaneously before reassembling them at the receiving end via a paired Vantablack decoder unit. The result is a signal profile that, to conventional intercept equipment, resembles nothing more coherent than ambient electromagnetic noise — radio ghost-chatter from old infrastructure, the static hiss of decaying city grid components.

What distinguishes the Shroud from competing signal-scatter systems is Vantablack's proprietary Chromatic Masking Layer, a passive analog component woven into the garment's lining that mimics the EM signature of the wearer's immediate environment. Near a power relay, the Shroud bleeds into the relay's hum. Near a corporate tower, it replicates the tower's passive emissions. This environmental mimicry is not digital — it cannot be patched out or remotely disabled — making the Shroud uniquely resilient against software-based spectrum sweeps.

The Shroud is a tool of journalists, fixers, and mid-tier syndicate coordinators who need persistent, low-detectability communication over extended operational periods rather than brief tactical bursts. Vantablack markets it obliquely through front distributors, framing it as 'signal privacy apparel' for executives concerned about corporate espionage — a fiction that provides useful legal cover while the product finds its true market in GLMZ's lower precincts.

specifications.active_range: Up to 4.2 km direct; up to 18 km via mesh relay node
specifications.power_source: Body-heat thermocouple array, 72-hour reserve cell backup

tactical_use: The Shroud is favored for long-duration operations where the operator must communicate repeatedly without establishing a detectable transmission pattern. Couriers use it to confirm drops without breaking stride. Field journalists use it to file dispatches from inside corporate exclusion zones. Because it requires no active device to hold or manipulate, it allows the user to appear entirely off-comms to visual surveillance while maintaining a live channel. Its primary limitation is latency — the reassembly process introduces a 1.2–2.8 second delay, making it unsuitable for real-time tactical coordination under fire.
cultural_context: In GLMZ's information underclass — the fixers, the stringers, the mid-level syndicate workers who can't afford full ghost implants — the Shroud occupies a particular cultural niche as a symbol of professional seriousness. Wearing one signals that you've moved past burner handsets and disposable mesh nodes, that you operate at a level where persistent, deniable communication is a necessity rather than a luxury. Among investigative journalists in particular, owning a Shroud is a quiet credential, passed between colleagues like a reference. Vantablack's own employees are rumored to use them internally when communicating outside sanctioned channels — a detail the company neither confirms nor denies.
known_users: Fixer networks operating in signal-dense precincts
story_hooks: A Shroud surfaces on a dead body — its paired decoder unit is still active and receiving, meaning someone is waiting for a transmission that will never come.
A player's Shroud begins mimicking a frequency profile that doesn't match any known local infrastructure — something is broadcasting nearby that shouldn't exist.

Vantablack quietly recalls a specific production batch of Shrouds, offering generous compensation and no questions. The batch numbers correspond to units distributed to a particular journalist collective six months before their silence.

A contact insists on meeting only via Shroud-channel, claiming that face-to-face or standard comms are already compromised — but the players have no way to verify whether the paranoia is justified or a setup.

The Chromatic Masking Layer on a black-market Shroud has been modified to mimic a specific corporate tower's EM signature — meaning any transmission through it will appear, to interceptors, to originate from inside that tower.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, form-fitting textile insert resembling a minimalist tactical vest liner or high-collar shirt insert. The outer surface appears as matte charcoal-black fabric with a subtle iridescent sheen that shifts when light catches it at oblique angles—the signature of embedded conductive mesh. The interior reveals densely woven filament architecture: copper-threaded conductor arrays interlaced with what appears to be graphene lattice, creating a visual texture reminiscent of circuit board traces translated into cloth. No visible digital display or controls; the device is entirely passive and haptic in operation.
physical_description.dimensions: Vest insert form factor, typically 45–55 cm in width when laid flat, 25–30 cm in height. Fits snugly against the torso beneath street clothing; collapses to pocket-sized when folded.
physical_description.weight_description: Handheld/wearable weight (340g). Light enough to wear under clothing for extended periods without fatigue; noticeable but unobtrusive during tactical movement.
physical_description.primary_material: Tri-layer composite: outer ballistic nylon weave treated with Vantablack proprietary coating, middle conductive mesh layer (copper and graphene filament), inner moisture-wicking polymer-silk blend housing the thermocouple array.
physical_description.finish: Matte absorption-black with micro-texture surface treatment that deadens reflectivity. Seams reinforced with silver-thread topstitching. The inner lining exhibits a faint honeycomb texture where thermocouple nodes interface with body heat.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: dead-flat black (EM-absorbing Vantablack treatment). Accent: minimal silver topstitching at seams and thermocouple interface points. Decoder pairing indicator uses discrete amber LED embedded in back-panel corner pocket.
physical_description.interface_elements: Zero visible interactive elements. Wearers interface via haptic feedback: a small rubberized patch on the right side permits fingertip calibration taps (frequency selection, pairing mode). Thermocouple array visible as subtle dimpled grid pattern on inner surface. Decoder pairing port hidden behind reinforced seam (micro-connector, proprietary standard).
distinctive_features: Iridescent sheen revealing embedded conductive mesh only when light strikes surface at acute angles
Visible graphene filament matrix creating circuit-board-like aesthetic on interior
Thermocouple node grid visually prominent on inner lining—evokes high-tech thermal mapping garment
Reinforced seams with silver topstitching suggest military/tactical provenance
Entirely seamless user interface—no buttons, screens, or visible controls; pure passive operation
Faint honeycomb microstructure pattern hinting at distributed EM mimicry sensory array
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Subtle Voss Signal Intelligence logo (minimalist stylized V in silver thread) embroidered inside back collar. Regulatory compliance stamps for GLMZ Tier 2+ signal architecture (small textile label, nearly invisible against black). Serial number printed in thermographic ink visible only under IR light. Care instructions in five languages reference 'signal privacy apparel for executive discretion'—the oblique marketing fiction.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn concealed beneath a work shirt, tech vest, or formal corporate layer. When visible (during changing or inspection), the black matte surface absorbs light dramatically—appears almost two-dimensional against surrounding environment. After extended wear, minor creasing visible at body contact points; no visible degradation to conductive mesh.
